watch-the-presentation.text: Watch the eleven-slide presentation here, or open the full-screen view. It begins with the real direction: the Singular registry supports an intended KERI consumer. Naming is the simpler surrogate application used to demonstrate that foundation. Every slide spells out a user role, a desired action and its purpose. Click inside the slides and use the arrow keys or navigation controls. Presenter mode, downloadable Markdown and speaker notes are available separately.

follow-alices-story.text: Follow Alice as she claims her name and gets it registered. When she changes wallets, she updates the payment destination while keeping the name. If she loses her controller key, she can recover using the next controller committed beforehand. She or her fixed retirement quorum can initiate retirement. After completion, nobody can reuse that name within the same registry.

the-preprod-demonstration.text: The preproduction run is pending. The demonstration will follow one real transaction sequence: claim a name, fold with its representative N F T, recover control, retire, and complete to Over. Transaction identifiers in the speaker notes remain pending until that connected run exists. External-node tooling alone does not establish the demonstration.

evidence-and-limits.text: The slides link to an exact model and validator revision. Speaker notes distinguish model propositions, source code and finite ledger execution. Existing development-network results are supporting material only. The demonstration must run on preproduction. Resolver services, wallet integration and mainnet deployment remain future work. Programmable values and a second KERI consumer are planned, not completed integration.
